(Cleveland, Ohio) | college = [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron]] (2019–2024) | draft_year = | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season rebounding leaders|NCAA season rebounds leader]] (2024) * [[Associated Press|AP]] honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2024 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2024]]) * [[Mid-American Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MAC Player of the Year]] (2024) * 2× First-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2023, 2024) * Second-team All-MAC (2022) * MAC Defensive Player of the Year (2022) * 4× MAC All-Defensive team (2021–2024) * 2× [[Mid-American Conference men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] MVP ([[2022 MAC men's basketball tournament|2022]], [[2024 MAC men's basketball tournament|2024]]) }} '''Enrique Gabriel Freeman''' (born July 29, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron Zips]]. ==College career== After a prep career at [[St. Martin de Porres High School (Cleveland)|St. Martin de Porres High School]] in [[Cleveland]], Freeman had no college basketball offers. He accepted an academic scholarship to the [[University of Akron]] and at the urging of friends and family, tried out for a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] spot with the school's basketball team, earning a roster spot. He played sparingly as a freshman, totaling 13 minutes on the season. He grew four inches between his first and second years and earned a scholarship and a starting role for the Zips. He earned his first [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) all-defensive team honor.{{cite web| last = Pluto| first = Terry | url = https://www.cleveland.com/sports/college/2023/09/meet-akrons-enrique-freeman-if-you-want-to-smile-read-this-story-terry-pluto.html | title = Meet Akron’s Enrique Freeman: If you want to smile, read this story – Terry Pluto | date = September 15, 2023| website = cleveland.com| publisher = [[Cleveland.com]] | access-date = January 2, 2024| quote = }} As Freeman established himself as one of the top defensive players in the MAC during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]], his offense began to develop as well. He averaged a [[double-double]] for the season and led the nation in [[field goal percentage]]. He earned second-team All-MAC honors and was named the conference Defensive Player of the Year. He led the Zips to a [[Mid-American Conference men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] title, and was named the tournament MVP.{{cite web| last = Beaven| first = Michael | url = https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/2022/03/16/enrique-freeman-akron-zips-ucla-ncaa-mens-basketball-tournament-east-region-john-groce-mac-champions/7032693001/ | title = 'I am here and it feels great': Enrique Freeman leads Akron into NCAA Tournament | date = March 16, 2022| website = beaconjournal.com| publisher = [[Akron Beacon Journal]] | access-date = January 2, 2024| quote = }} Following the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]], Freeman declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] but retained his college eligibility. He worked out for several teams but ultimately decided to return to Akron for his senior season.{{cite web| last = Thomas| first = George M. | url = https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/college/zips/2023/05/31/akron-zips-forward-enrique-freeman-pulls-name-from-nba-draft/70274479007/ | title = Report: Akron Zips forward Enrique Freeman
